documents.title: Generative Artificial Intelligence (GAI) Course Policy
tiers: Option 2: Generative AI Permitted with Specific Limits
Option 3: Generative AI Permitted with Disclosure and Reflection
documents.summary: A template course policy offering instructors three options: no generative AI, AI for listed purposes only, or AI with disclosure and reflection. It adds shared responsibilities for students and instructors and notes Turnitin and writing-process evidence.
documents.stance_why: The document sets no single stance; it says '[Choose which option from 1-3 fits your course]' and supplies three tiers from a ban to open use with disclosure, so the decision is delegated to instructors.

units.why: Opens by framing GAI as 'technologies you may encounter in school, work, and everyday life', a scope statement that sets what the policy covers; it informs rather than directs, so P61 (define AI and scope).
units.anchor: tools are technologies you may encounter in school, work, and everyday life

units.why: A definition of what GAI tools produce ('text, images, code, audio, or other content'), setting policy coverage; definitional, so informs and P61.
units.anchor: These tools can generate text, images, code, audio, or other content in response to prompts

units.why: States that 'outputs may be inaccurate, biased, incomplete, or misleading', a warning that output is unreliable. P31 (verify AI output) fits better than P53 because the concern is output quality, not societal harm.
units.anchor: their outputs may be inaccurate, biased, incomplete, or misleading

units.why: 'You are responsible for demonstrating your own learning' makes students accountable for their work, so P29 and must. The clause on following integrity, privacy and accessibility policies is a general reference, folded into this unit.
units.anchor: You are responsible for demonstrating your own learning

units.why: The template tells instructors to 'Choose which option from 1-3', a menu of named tiers (not permitted / specific limits / disclosure and reflection), so P05. P04 also fits, but the defining feature here is the named three-option menu.
units.anchor: Choose which option from 1-3 fits your course

units.why: 'You may update and change specifics as needed' lets each instructor adapt the template per course, so the rule is set per instructor: P04.
units.anchor: You may update and change specifics as needed
units.policy: Instructors may update and change the specifics of the chosen option as needed.

units.why: Option 1 states 'you may not use generative artificial intelligence tools', a blanket default ban for the course, so P01 and must-not.
units.anchor: you may not use generative artificial intelligence tools

units.why: 'All submitted work must be created by you, without assistance from AI tools' bars AI-generated submissions across writing, analysis, problem-solving and content generation; P19 chosen over P29 since the rule is specifically about AI producing the work.
units.anchor: All submitted work must be created by you, without assistance from AI tools

units.why: Extends the ban to 'AI-generated content created by someone else ... even if you did not personally use the tool', closing a loophole about who ran the AI; still about not submitting AI-produced work, P19.
units.anchor: submitting AI-generated content created by someone else

units.why: Gives the reason for the ban: goals of 'developing independent thinking, foundational skills, and original intellectual work'. P42 (fundamentals first) vs P41 (AI shortcuts practice): the emphasis on foundational skills fits P42.
units.anchor: developing independent thinking, foundational skills, and original intellectual work

units.why: 'These skills take time and practice to build' explains that the practice itself builds skill, which AI use would shortcut; P41.
units.anchor: These skills take time and practice to build

units.why: Classifies impermissible AI use as 'an academic integrity concern' handled under 'university procedures', which is P36.
units.anchor: is an academic integrity concern and will be addressed in accordance with university procedures

units.why: Option 1 exempts 'approved accommodations that involve assistive technologies' from the restriction; an access/accommodation carve-out, so P51.
units.anchor: Approved accommodations that involve assistive technologies are not restricted by this policy

units.why: Template note that the shared-responsibility text belongs to 'Options 2 and 3' and not Option 1; it structures the tiered template, so P05 (a minor structural unit).
units.anchor: Options 2 and 3 Additional Text

units.why: 'You are responsible for submitting work that reflects your own thinking, learning, and effort' puts ownership of submissions on the student: P29.
units.anchor: You are responsible for submitting work that reflects your own thinking, learning, and effort

units.why: Where AI is permitted, 'I expect you to use them thoughtfully and ethically' sets a general expectation of judgment. P32 (student remains thinker) is closest; no type covers generic ethical use.
units.anchor: I expect you to use them thoughtfully and ethically

units.why: 'Follow the AI guidelines for this course and each assignment' ties rules to the specific course and assignment, so P11 rather than P04 because it addresses student compliance.
units.anchor: Follow the AI guidelines for this course and each assignment

units.why: 'Disclose any permitted use of generative AI' is a direct disclosure duty: P24.
units.anchor: Disclose any permitted use of generative AI

units.why: 'Check the accuracy of any AI-influenced content' requires verification of output: P31.
units.anchor: Check the accuracy of any AI-influenced content

units.why: 'Make sure your work reflects your understanding' requires students to understand what they submit. P30 chosen over P29 since the focus is understanding, though it does not say 'explain every line'.
units.anchor: Make sure your work reflects your understanding

units.why: Even where AI is permitted, students must 'Not submit AI-generated content created by someone else'; this bars submitting AI output not produced by the student as their work: P19.
units.anchor: Not submit AI-generated content created by someone else

units.why: The instructor is 'responsible for clearly explaining how generative AI may or may not be used', an obligation to state expectations: P09.
units.anchor: clearly explaining how generative AI may or may not be used in this course

units.why: The instructor is also responsible for 'designing assignments that support learning'; a vague commitment to assignment design, nearest to P35.
units.anchor: designing assignments that support learning

units.why: 'Explaining AI expectations in the syllabus and assignments' says where expectations must be stated: P09.
units.anchor: Explaining AI expectations in the syllabus and assignments

units.why: The instructor commits to 'Using tools like Turnitin responsibly', a similarity/AI-analysis tool for review: P40. P39 does not fit since detectors are not disclaimed.
units.anchor: Using tools like Turnitin responsibly

units.why: 'Looking at context and your explanation if questions arise' commits the instructor to hear the student before concluding misuse. P57 chosen over P64 because it is framed as instructor practice.
units.anchor: Looking at context and your explanation if questions arise

units.why: 'Some assignments may be submitted through Turnitin' tells students of a similarity-check tool in use: P40.
units.anchor: Some assignments may be submitted through Turnitin

units.why: Students agree by enrolling to 'text-matching and AI-related analysis features', i.e. AI analysis of submissions to identify misuse: P40.
units.anchor: including text-matching and AI-related analysis features

units.why: 'I may use Turnitin as one way to review submissions' permits the instructor to use a checking tool, framed as only 'one way', so P40.
units.anchor: I may use Turnitin as one way to review submissions

units.why: The instructor 'may ask to see drafts, revision histories, or notes' as process evidence when questions arise: P40. P26 is a student-side submission duty and does not fit.
units.anchor: I may ask to see drafts, revision histories, or notes

units.why: Option 2 allows AI 'only for specific purposes and/or on specific assignments, as outlined by your instructor': narrow listed uses (restrict) decided per instructor and assignment, so P04 rather than P02.
units.anchor: only for specific purposes and/or on specific assignments, as outlined by your instructor

units.why: 'they should not replace your own thinking, problem-solving, or writing' keeps the student as primary thinker: P32.
units.anchor: they should not replace your own thinking, problem-solving, or writing

units.why: Suggested permitted use 'Brainstorming ideas or exploring possible approaches', exactly P15.
units.anchor: Brainstorming ideas or exploring possible approaches

units.why: Suggested permitted use 'Grammar, clarity, or style suggestions' is prose-level help: P18.
units.anchor: Grammar, clarity, or style suggestions

units.why: 'Outline development or early planning' is idea and structure generation, closest to P15 (brainstorming and exploring approaches).
units.anchor: Outline development or early planning

units.why: Suggested prohibited use 'Having AI write full assignments or responses for you': P19.
units.anchor: Having AI write full assignments or responses for you

units.why: Option 2's list of prohibited uses restates the ban on submitting AI content made by another person; coded for this option's own text as P19.
units.anchor: Submitting AI-generated content created by someone else

units.why: Suggested prohibition on 'Completing graded problem-solving tasks using AI'; AI doing graded tasks is P19.
units.anchor: Completing graded problem-solving tasks using AI

units.why: Suggested prohibition on 'Summarizing assigned course readings unless explicitly permitted'. Summaries fall under P14's coverage (summaries as study aids), here forbidden unless permitted, so P14 is where a reader would look.
units.anchor: Summarizing assigned course readings unless explicitly permitted

units.why: 'All other uses of GAI not specified as permitted or previously discussed with me' bans anything unlisted, a fallback rule: P06 (it also implies asking first, P10, but the default ban is the main point).
units.anchor: All other uses of GAI not specified as permitted

units.why: 'Submitting work created by someone else or by an AI system as if it were your own work is not allowed' is a ban on passing off AI work: P19.
units.anchor: by an AI system as if it were your own work is not allowed

units.why: 'Using generative AI does not shift responsibility away from you' keeps responsibility with the student: P29.
units.anchor: Using generative AI does not shift responsibility away from you

units.why: 'You remain the author of your work' asserts ownership of submissions; a separate statement from the responsibility sentence, P29.
units.anchor: You remain the author of your work

units.why: 'you must include a brief disclosure statement with your assignment' is the Option 2 disclosure duty: P24.
units.anchor: you must include a brief disclosure statement with your assignment

units.why: 'Failure to disclose permitted GAI is an academic integrity violation' makes nondisclosure itself the violation: P28 (Option 2 instance).
units.anchor: Failure to disclose permitted GAI is an academic integrity violation

units.why: Students must ensure 'the final work reflects your own understanding, effort, and learning'; understanding focus, P30.
units.anchor: the final work reflects your own understanding, effort, and learning

units.why: Option 2 repeats the accommodation exemption; coded because Option 2 is a separate tier, P51.
units.anchor: Approved accommodations that involve assistive technologies are not restricted by this policy

units.why: Option 3 allows AI 'as long as you are open and transparent', a permissive default with a disclosure condition: P02.
units.anchor: as long as you are open and transparent about how you use them

units.why: 'If you use GAI at any stage of your work, you must include a short disclosure': P24.
units.anchor: you must include a short disclosure

units.why: The disclosure must say 'Which tool(s) you used', a named detail required in the citation: P25.
units.anchor: Which tool(s) you used

units.why: The disclosure must explain 'How you used the tool'; specific detail on use, P25.
units.anchor: How you used the tool

units.why: The disclosure must give 'Why you chose to use it', a reflection on the AI use rather than a citation detail: P26 (reflections).
units.anchor: Why you chose to use it

units.why: The disclosure must note 'limitations, inaccuracies, or concerns you noticed in the output', a critical reflection: P26 over P31 because it is a submitted reflection.
units.anchor: Any limitations, inaccuracies, or concerns you noticed in the output

units.why: Disclosure 'should appear as a clearly labeled section or appendix with your submission', placement of the statement: P24 (P27 concerns marking code at its use point, which this is not).
units.anchor: a clearly labeled section or appendix with your submission

units.why: 'You must submit work that reflects your own thinking and learning' requires the work be the student's own: P29.
units.anchor: You must submit work that reflects your own thinking and learning

units.why: Even under Option 3, 'presenting AI-generated content as if it were entirely your own, is not permitted': P19.
units.anchor: presenting AI-generated content as if it were entirely your own, is not permitted

units.why: Option 3 repeats that nondisclosure is a violation; coded as a separate unit because it governs a different tier, P28.
units.anchor: Failure to disclose permitted GAI is an academic integrity violation

units.why: Option 3 carries the same accommodations exemption, P51.
units.anchor: Approved accommodations that involve assistive technologies are not restricted by this policy

notes: Single university-level template document; no school or computing policy found. Repeated exemption and nondisclosure sentences are coded once per option because each option is a separate tier. Topic tags are free-form (no AGENT_BRIEF.md found).
